preamble: Deaffrication (spirantization) of the voiced alveolo-palatal affricate [dʑ] to the fricative [ʑ]. In Standard Japanese the voiced alveolo-palatal sibilant (from /z/ or /d/ before /i/ and /j/) is an affricate [dʑ] after a pause and after the moraic nasal or geminate, but between vowels it is commonly a fricative [ʑ]: 文字 'letter' is /mod͡ʑi/ ~ [mo̞ʑi] (with [d͡ʑ] after the nasal in the variant [mõ̞ɲ̟d͡ʑi]), 火事 'fire' [ka̠ʑi], against initial [d͡ʑ] in 柔道 [d͡ʑɨːdo̞ː]. Maekawa's corpus study of spontaneous Japanese found affricate realizations about 80% of the time after a pause, 74% after /Q/ and 60% after /N/, with fricative realizations increasing at faster speech rates.
context: Between vowels, especially in fast speech; the affricate [dʑ] is favoured after a pause and after the moraic nasal or a geminate

examples.note: Intervocalic; the nasal-preceded variant monji keeps the affricate [mõ̞ɲ̟d͡ʑi].
Wikipedia gives [ka̠ʑi] and notes [ʑ] is in free variation with [d͡ʑ] between vowels.
Example given in Wikipedia's Japanese phonology article.

sources: Maekawa, K. (2010). Coarticulatory reinterpretation of allophonic variation: Corpus-based analysis of /z/ in spontaneous Japanese. Journal of Phonetics 38(3), 360–374. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wocn.2010.03.001
